hypothesis: If the claim holds, then in sunflower capitula the two families of contact-parastichy spirals cross at a roughly constant angle across the disc, with the angle set by the divergence angle and the radial scaling rather than fixed at 90 degrees. Orthogonal crossings should then be a minority of capitula, and in those capitula only a narrow band of radii should be near-orthogonal.
pass_criterion: Using seed-centre coordinates (x, y) from at least 30 mature capitula, fit logarithmic spirals to each parastichy family and compute the local crossing angle of the two families at every seed. The claim is supported if both of these hold. (a) Within a capitulum, the crossing angle is isogonal: the coefficient of variation of the angle across radii from 20% to 90% of the disc radius is at most 0.15. (b) Fewer than 25% of capitula have a median crossing angle within 90 ± 5 degrees.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if either of these holds. (a) The within-capitulum crossing angle varies systematically with radius, with a coefficient of variation above 0.30 or a monotonic trend that the fitted logarithmic spirals do not explain. (b) At least 50% of capitula have a median crossing angle within 90 ± 5 degrees, so that orthogonality is common rather than infrequent.
interpretation: Thompson's 'spirals' are the visible contact parastichies, one family running clockwise and one counter-clockwise. 'Isogonal' means a constant crossing angle, which is the defining property of logarithmic spirals about a common pole. 'Orthogonal' means a 90 degree crossing, the case Church argued for. The measurable quantities are the angle between the tangents of the two fitted parastichy families at each seed, and its variation with radius. The modern reinterpretation is that real capitula follow Vogel's model, in which the radius goes as the square root of the seed index. The parastichies are then not exact logarithmic spirals, and the crossing angle drifts from near-orthogonal at the periphery toward a smaller angle near the centre. The test therefore uses a tolerance, not exact constancy.
no_dataset_reason: I could not verify any public dataset of seed-centre coordinates or parastichy crossing angles for sunflower capitula that has a landing page and a DOI I am sure of. The general portals I know well (GBIF, iDigBio, NHANES, DATRAS, FishBase) hold specimen records and images but no extracted phyllotactic geometry. Naming a half-remembered paper supplement risks inventing an identifier, so I am returning null. The test would need a new image-derived dataset, for example capitulum photographs with segmented seed positions.
